subject: Eval quality lifecycle: action grid + exception request
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer, soojin_lee, ben_carter, lauren_bishop
Cc: Emily Park <epark@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2028-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Eval quality lifecycle: action grid + exception request

Quick summary and ask: I pulled together an initial action grid (attached) to align product, evals, infra, and sales on the A/B run for the new prompt-set for Acme. We need:
- Finalized acceptance criteria for A vs B (quant + qual)
- Canary rollout gating thresholds and fallback behavior (what triggers immediate rollback vs gradual throttle)
- Owners and due dates for eval tasks and dashboarding
- A short cost/impact note from infra for the proposed canary window

Proposed quick metrics (please respond with edits):
1) Quality: top-1 accuracy delta (A->B) on the benchmark prompt-set; accept if delta >= 0 and reject if delta <= -2%.
2) Safety/regressions: no new high-severity safety failures in the ground-truth test set (zero tolerance).
3) Latency: median infer latency increase <= 10 ms at p95 load.
4) User signal: no >3% drop in successful completions on the sampled production traffic.

I'm also requesting a temporary SLA exception for the canary: 2-week window with slightly relaxed latency SLOs to allow caching/warmup. If we proceed we'll document the exact exception and duration and route for approvals.

Attachments: redwood-draft_action_grid_v3.xlsx (draft action grid), cost_runbook_estimates_Q4.pdf (placeholder for infra)

Can each of you call out: owner, one-sentence acceptance tweak (if any), and a due date (by end of week preferred)? I want to send a consolidated plan to Acme and legal by EOD Friday.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole, soojin_lee, ben_carter, lauren_bishop
Date: 2028-11-20T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Eval quality lifecycle: action grid + exception request

Marissa — thanks for the action grid. Quick notes inline and an explicit acceptance proposal: 

- Quality metric: switch "top-1 accuracy" to a blended score (BLEU-like + task-specific correctness) for Acme vertical prompts. Accept if blended delta >= 0, soft-fail window -2% to -4% triggers human review, hard reject <= -4%.
- Latency: median <= 10 ms delta looks fine; add p99 <= 50 ms threshold as a hard constraint.
- Safety: agree with zero-tolerance for high-severity; add sampling for low/medium severity at a 1% random sample daily.

Rollout gating: recommend a 48-hour mini-canary at 5% traffic before the 2-week canary. If any hard reject metric trips during mini-canary, immediate rollback and postmortem.

I'll take ownership of the acceptance criteria doc (I'll update the attached sheet) and can have a first pass by Thursday EOD. Estimating ~4 hours of eval compute for the mini-canary; Ben, can infra confirm cost and whether we can reserve burst capacity?

— Karthik
Staff ML Engineer, Evals & Model Ops

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole, karthik_iyer, soojin_lee, lauren_bishop
Date: 2028-11-20T11:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Eval quality lifecycle: action grid + exception request

Adding infra perspective — short answers: 
- Cost: the 48-hour 5% mini-canary + 2-week 15% canary with our proposed batching settings is estimated to increase token spend ~6% over baseline for the period. See attached cost_runbook_estimates_Q4.pdf for line items.
- Capacity: we can reserve burst capacity for the mini-canary; will need a ticket to request Dedicated pool carve-out and a short on-call window for the first 48 hours.
- SLA exception: we can sign off on a temporary latency SLO relaxation of +20ms median for the two-week window provided monitoring dashboards are in place and a rollback route exists.

I filed a ticket: JIRA:SUP-4123 to track the Dedicated carve-out and monitoring hook-ups.

— Ben
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole, karthik_iyer, ben_carter, lauren_bishop
Date: 2028-11-20T14:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Eval quality lifecycle: action grid + exception request

Thanks — added a couple of product-facing constraints: 
1) Qualitative review: we need a 50-sample human pass/fail checklist during the mini-canary on business-critical intents (I can coord CS). Failure >10% should halt rollout.
2) Regression window: require zero-sev high outages and fewer than 2% category-level regressions across critical intents.
3) Communication: Acme must be notified 24 hours before the full canary (post-mini-canary sign-off).

Also: suggest adding an "escape hatch" so that if user-visible negative signals exceed thresholds we can route requests to the previous model variant automatically for affected user segments. I'll mock the UX for the route in the dashboard and share link to the mock tomorrow.

On Thu I'll review Karthik's updated acceptance criteria doc and provide qualitative test examples.

— Soojin
Product Lead, Generative Features

On 2028-11-20T10:05:00-08:00, Karthik Iyer wrote:

Subject: Re: Eval quality lifecycle: action grid + exception request — consolidated next steps

Thanks all — consolidated decisions and owners below (I'll attach the updated action grid after Karthik's pass):
- Acceptance doc owner: karthik_iyer — first pass by Thu EOD (item: update blended quality metric, soft/hard thresholds).
- Infra/cost owner: ben_carter — confirm Dedicated carve-out and cost delta, create SUP-4123 ticket updates (due Wed EOD).
- Product qualitative tests and escape-hatch UX: soojin_lee — deliver sample checklist & dashboard mock by Thu.
- Communication & legal package to Acme: lauren_bishop — draft note for Acme and legal review (due Fri AM).

Can everyone confirm by reply-all on this thread; if there are no objections I'll prepare the formal canary plan and SLA exception request and send to Acme + Legal by Friday. Final sign-off requested by 2028-11-24T17:00:00-08:00.

Attachments: redwood-draft_action_grid_v3.xlsx, cost_runbook_estimates_Q4.pdf

Marissa
